# Team News: South Korea vs Czech Republic injury, suspension list, predicted XIs | World Cup 2026

By Jonathan O'Shea| 10 Jun 2026 03:00, Last updated: 10 Jun 2026 20:23

© Imago

Getting under way in Guadalajara, both South Korea and the Czech Republic will commence their Group A campaign at World Cup 2026 when they meet on Thursday.

While the Taegeuk Warriors strolled through Asian qualifying their Czech counterparts came through two UEFA playoff rounds on penalties to make it to North America.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up the latest team news for both sides.

## Czechia team news
[...]
This marks Czechia’s first appearance at a World Cup since 2006, and they arrive with a well-balanced and settled squad.
[...]
A major boost for the team is the return of attacking midfielder Adam Hložek, who has recovered from long-term calf and foot injuries in time to be included.
[...]
Head coach Miroslav Koubek has almost a full squad available, giving him the flexibility to stick to his preferred physical approach to the game. The team will depend heavily on players from the Premier League and Bundesliga to take control in key areas.
[...]
Midfielder Tomáš Souček of West Ham is fully fit and will play a crucial role in controlling the midfield and supporting the defense.
[...]
In attack, Bayer Leverkusen striker Patrik Schick is in excellent form and will lead the frontline. Overall, Czechia looks strongorganiseded, and ready to use their physical presence to push for an important win in their opening match.
[...]

[...]
Possible Czechia starting XI: Kovar; Chaloupek, Hranac, Krejci; Coufal, Cerv, Soucek, Jurasek; Provod, Sulc; Schick

results.title: Czechia lineup vs South Korea confirmed for FIFA World Cup 2026 clash
highlights:
# Czechia lineup vs South Korea confirmed for FIFA World Cup 2026 clash
[...]
South Korea confirmed
[...]
## Czechia take on South Korea in the FIFA World Cup 2026 tonight.
[...]
Czechia will mark their return to the World Cup after an absence of two decades when they take on Asian giants South Korea in a crucial Group A fixture at Estadio Akron. The Narod’ak will look to improve upon their group stage exit in 2006 in the expanded FIFA World Cup 2026 in North America.
[...]
The Ladislav Krejci-led side are making only their second appearance in FIFA’s flagship tournament as an independent nation. They will be looking to make a good impression against a strong South Korean national team featuring the likes of Son Heung-min.
[...]
Despite their poor record in the tournament, Czechia have been in good form of late, beating Kosovo and Guatemala in the World Cup warm-up friendlies. Head coach Miroslav Koubek will hope that his side can carry that form into their opening match against the Taegeuk Warriors.
[...]
### Let’s look at the Czechia predicted lineup for the FIFA World Cup 2026 match against South Korea:
[...]
Czechia (3-4-2-1): Matej Kovar; Tomas Holes, Robin Hranac, Ladislav Krejci; Vladimir Coufal, Tomas Soucek, Michal Sadilek, David Jurasek; Lukas Provod, Pavel Sulc; Patrik Schick
[...]
### Thoughts on the Czechia lineup
[...]
Bayer Leverkusen striker Patrik Schick is the star man for Czechia. He has scored 26 goals for the national team, including five in the World Cup qualifiers. As a result, Koubek will stick with him as the lone striker.
[...]
Lyon star Pavel Sulc will be the creative outlet for the team, and he will be joined by Slavia Prague attacker Lukas Provod. Former captain Tomas Soucek, who is the most experienced member of the Czech squad, will anchor the midfield along with defensive midfielder Michal Sadilek. Lukas Cerv or Vladimir Darida can also take Sadilek’s place.
[...]
David Jurasek and Vladimir Coufal will start in the wing-back positions. Captain Ladislav Krejci will start in the three-man defence, along with Hoffenheim’s Robin Hranac and Slavia veteran Tomas Holes.
[...]
PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar, who was a hero for his nation during the European play-offs, will start between the sticks.
[...]
The Group A clash will be played on June 11, 2026, at Estadio Akron in Guadalajara, Mexico. In India, the match will kick off at 7:30 AM IST on June 12.

results.title: Czech Republic's 3-4-3 Lineup: Changes Possible
highlights:
The Czech Republic, which had been tightly concealing its strategies, finally unveils its plans. During the European playoffs, they made minimal changes to their lineup. Their base formation was 3-4-3, occasionally shifting to 3-4-2-1 depending on the forward positioning. Since many players who participated in the European playoffs were included in the final roster, their starting lineup against South Korea is expected to be similar.
[...]
The sports media outlet *Illustrated* predicted the Czech Republic would use a 3-4-3 tactic against South Korea. They anticipated Macej Kobarsi (Aintohoben) as the goalkeeper. The three defenders were expected to be captain Radislav Krejchi (Olbeohamteon), Robin Hranyachi (Hoffenheim), and Tomas Holesi (Slavia Prague). The midfielders were Vladimir Choupal (Hoffenheim), Vladimir Darida (Hradec Kralove), Tomas Soucek (West Ham), and David Yurasek (Sparta Prague). The forwards were Patrik Sik (Leverkusen), Adam Hlozek (Hoffenheim), and Lukas Provod (Slavia Prague). The statistics company Squawka made a similar prediction but expected Pavel Schulz (Lyon) instead of Provod in the attack.
[...]
The overall framework remains unchanged. Sik in attack, Soucek in midfield, Krejchi in defense, and Kobarsi in goal are expected to lead the game. There are conflicting views on some positions. Miroslav Koubek, the Czech World Cup team coach, was expected to recheck the starting lineup through a final mock game against Guatemala (3-1 win). However, after the Guatemala match, he said, 'It’s good to have considerations,' and encouraged competition until the end, stating, 'Players who entered in the second half showed good performances.' In the Guatemala match, Sik, Schulz, and Provod started. Schulz played 45 minutes before being replaced by Hlozek, and Provod was substituted with Tomas Hori (Slavia Prague) in the 17th minute of the second half. Additionally, Koubek alternated between Holesi and Stefan Chalupka (Slavia Prague) for the right center-back position. Depending on the final competition results, one or two positions might change. Notably, the match is expected to be a water battle. The Czech team, which trained in high temperatures, might adjust to the sudden environmental change.
